narrative_purpose: The chapter's representative plate on the landing book-map: Pandora seen whole from space as a single living organism — the moon as one luminous, breathing body, the synthesis image that closes Part III and asks whether a planet can itself be alive.
subject: The full disc of the habitable moon Pandora seen from orbit against deep space, the gas giant Polyphemus a vast banded presence behind it, the moon's night side threaded all over with the faintest web of glowing bioluminescent filaments — forests, coastlines and ocean alike laced into one continuous shimmering circuit, so the whole world reads as a single wired organism rather than a dead rock with life on top.
scene: A wide orbital view: the moon hanging in space, half lit by its distant sun, the dark hemisphere alive with a planet-spanning lattice of cool light, the curve of Polyphemus filling the upper background.
camera: A distant orbital establishing shot, the whole disc of the moon in frame, deep space around it.
light: A soft rim of sunlight on one limb; the dark side self-lit from within by the cool bioluminescent network; deep space black elsewhere.
palette: Void-indigo space, the moon's living network in Pandora cyan and living teal, Polyphemus in muted storm-band tones behind.
style: Painterly speculative-astronomy naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, luminous and atmospheric.
detail_level: Crisp on the moon's glowing network and limb; Polyphemus and space softer and atmospheric.
composition: The moon's disc set off-centre, the glowing network filling it, Polyphemus curving across one corner, generous dark space for the plate to breathe.
consistency_notes: Na'vi absent; landscape/astronomy plate. Cool Pandora palette with from-within bioluminescent key. The establishing 'the whole moon is one living system' mood that anchors the chapter.
